claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was born in Ibora in the Roman province of Pontus around 345 AD and died in the Nitrian Desert of Egypt in 399 AD.
He served as a deacon in Constantinople before abandoning his ecclesiastical career to become a monk in Jerusalem and later in the Egyptian desert.
The Thirty‑Three Chapters (Capitula xxxiii) are a collection of short treatises that define the passions of the rational soul by allegorically interpreting physical ailments.
After Evagrius’s death his teachings were later judged heterodox by some branches of the church, especially because of their Origenist elements.
The text survives in the Greek Patrologia Graeca (Migne) edition, available in modern digital PDFs such as the 1 MB file on Documenta Catholica Omnia.
